messages:
maria-chen: heads up — saw routing mismatch on staging: requests with X-Tenant-ID=acme sometimes hit default pool instead of dedicated shard. reproducible with curl.
ashok: ah — are those requests coming with an additional User-Agent override? last time UA heuristics bumped precedence.
maria-chen: good call. example request:
```
GET /v1/generate
Host: api.staging.redwood.test
X-Tenant-ID: acme
User-Agent: Redwood-CLI/1.2 (platform=web)
Authorization: Bearer sk.staging...
```
ashok: hmm we currently apply routing precedence: signed-auth > x-tenant-signed > x-tenant > user-agent > fallback. if the auth bearer maps to a different customer (token aliasing), it wins. can you paste the incoming auth claim?
maria-chen: token is a service token for our test harness; claim.sub=svc-harness, not acme. so it falls to auth first. the problem is the console rollout set a flag to prefer x-tenant for dedicated opt-ins, but the gateway config didn't pick it up.
jamie-l: this is the UX gap I flagged — console shows "Routing hint applied: X-Tenant-ID" for the request example, but it doesn't show the computed precedence or the effective route. customers get confused. can we expose the final decision in the request detail panel (non-sensitive)? :thinking_face:
nana-sre: telemetry shows a small spike in 403/404 when CDNs strip custom headers. we should add a metric: header-drop-rate per edge POP and a tag for "header-origin" (browser/proxy/curl). that will help triage when x-tenant is present but removed before hit.
nashok: agree on metric. also proposal: add a deterministic tie-breaker order for unauthenticated requests: prefer signed x-tenant header if present, else UA mapping. but for authenticated tokens, token-to-tenant mapping must be authoritative unless an allowlist override is set.
maria-chen: +1. but we also need a safe rollout path. Suggest feature-flagged gateway behavior: 
- default: current precedence (auth wins)
- opt-in: prefer x-tenant when header is signed or comes from trusted edge
rollout via console with per-tenant toggle, show audit log of decisions.
jamie-l: for console design: add an inline badge on the routing view: "Decision: auth (token->svc-harness) — override available" and a small "Why" flyout listing header values and signatures. keep PII out of view.
nana-sre: about header signing: can we reuse the existing route-signer key material? we need to track TTL and revocation — add a telemetry dimension for "signed-header-valid" true/false.
nashok: yes reuse route-signer. implementation detail: verify X-Tenant-Signature signature over canonicalized header string. fallback to UA if signature invalid. log signature failures to a low-sampled debug sink to avoid volume.
console-bot: rollout-note: updated routing-precedence feature flag created for staging (ff/routing_precedence/2025-11). canary policy: 10% of requests in staging, then 2% in prod.
maria-chen: thanks — I'll run smoke tests with service token vs tenant-signed header and capture the console trace.
nashok: quick patch idea — when header and token disagree and header is signed+valid, add a telemetry counter "header_vs_token_conflict" with labels { tenant_header, token_tenant, decision }. this will help us evaluate opt-in safety.
jamie-l: and please add console UX to surface that metric trend per-tenant for rollout. product wants alpha for next week.
nana-sre: also add quota implication: if header is used to route to dedicated pool, ensure quota checks use the tenant from the effective route, not the claims in the token. that was a previous footgun.
maria-chen: noted. I'll open a small RFC and attach smoke test logs.
deploy-bot: routing-config v1.12 deployed to staging at 2051234582 by ashok — successful.
maria-chen: verified on staging after deploy: when header is signed and token maps to different tenant, decision=header, console shows 'override: header (signed)'. tests for CDN-strip scenario failing though — file a bug?
nana-sre: file it here or in infra-ticketing. include edge POP and whether request used gzip/proxy.
maria-chen: filing now. thanks all. :tada:
